title: Wave 14: Lives of the Prophets, Bochart/Targums, Thucydides/Polybius, Caesar/Mascou, Francke Indian Tibet & European Chronicles

nodes.name: Prophet Hosea of Belemoth (Tribe of Issachar)
nodes.role: Twelve Minor Prophets & Tribesman of Issachar (Lives of Prophets)
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Lives of the Prophets locates Hosea at Belemoth in Issachar and records his burial in his homeland.

nodes.name: Prophet Micah the Morashtite (Tribe of Ephraim)
nodes.role: Judean-Ephraimite Prophet Slain by Joram (Lives of Prophets)
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Lives of the Prophets distinguishes Morasthi Micah's confrontation with Ahab's house and burial at Morasthi.

nodes.name: Prophet Amos of Tekoa (Herdsman of Judah)
nodes.role: Prophet of Tekoa Struck by Amaziah's Son at Bethel
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Profiled in Lives of the Prophets returning wounded from Bethel to expire and be buried with his fathers in Tekoa.

nodes.name: Prophet Joel ben Pethuel of Bethom (Tribe of Reuben)
nodes.role: Reubenite Prophet in Lives of the Prophets
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Attributed to the territory of Reuben at Bethom / Beth-meon in the Greek Lives of the Prophets.

nodes.name: Prophet Obadiah of Bethacharam near Shechem
nodes.role: Third Captain Under Elijah & Disciple Prophet of Shechem
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Identified in SBLMS1 as the third captain spared by Elijah on Carmel who later prophesied against Edom.

nodes.name: Prophet Jonah ben Amittai (+ Widow's Son Tradition)
nodes.role: Galilean Prophet of Gath-hepher & Nineveh Envoy
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Lives of the Prophets connects Jonah to the widow of Zarephath, Elijah's ministry, and Tyre/Nineveh.

nodes.name: Prophet Nahum of Elkesi & Nineveh Oracle
nodes.role: Prophet of Simeonite Elkosh
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Lives of the Prophets assigns Nahum to Simeon ('beyond Bethgabri') foretelling Nineveh's inundation.

nodes.name: Prophet Habakkuk of Bethzocher (Simeon)
nodes.role: Simeonite Watchman Prophet & Ostrakine Sojourner
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Fled Nebuchadnezzar to Ostrakine before returning to Judea; also featured in Bel and the Dragon.

nodes.name: Prophets Haggai, Zechariah & Malachi (Restored Temple Trio)
nodes.role: Post-Exilic Minor Prophets of Jerusalem
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Lives of the Prophets places Haggai's burial near the priests, Zechariah ben Berechiah beside him, and Malachi at Sofa in Zebulun.

nodes.name: Court Prophets Nathan, Ahijah the Shilonite & Azariah ben Oded
nodes.role: Royal Prophets of David, Solomon & Asa (Lives Ch. 17-20)
sources: The Lives of the Prophets (SBLMS1 / C.C. Torrey)
nodes.notes: Included in SBLMS1's extended canon of prophets: Nathan of Gabaon, Ahijah of Shiloh, and Azariah of Subatha.

nodes.name: Baruch ben Neriah (2 Baruch / Syriac Apocalypse)
nodes.role: Scribe of Jeremiah & Author of 2 Baruch / Paraleipomena
sources: R.H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Charles Vol. 2 preserves 2 Baruch's vision of twelve bright/dark waters and Baruch's epistles to the 9.5 exiled tribes.

nodes.name: Shealtiel / Salathiel & Eagle Vision (4 Ezra / 2 Esdras)
nodes.role: Royal Exilic Visionary in R.H. Charles Vol. 2
sources: R.H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Opens 4 Ezra ('In the thirtieth year after the ruin of our city, I Salathiel who am also Ezra, was in Babylon').

nodes.name: Aristeas & the 72 Septuagint Elders (Eleazar of Jerusalem)
nodes.role: Royal Envoy of Ptolemy II Philadelphus & Alexandrian Translators
sources: R.H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Letter of Aristeas (Charles Vol. 2) lists six elders from each of Israel's twelve tribes dispatched by High Priest Eleazar.

nodes.name: Martyrdom & Ascension of Isaiah (+ Balkira of Samaria)
nodes.role: Prophetic Martyrdom Under King Manasseh (Charles Vol. 2)
sources: R.H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Narrates Isaiah's flight to Bethlehem and martyrdom in the reign of Manasseh alongside his son Josab.

nodes.name: Elder Eleazar & the Seven Maccabean Brothers + Mother (4 Maccabees)
nodes.role: Antiochene Martyrs & Exemplars in Charles Vol. 2
sources: R.H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Recounts the philosophical martyrdom of Eleazar, Hannah/Solomone, and her seven sons during the Hasmonean revolt.

nodes.name: Sambethe (The Jewish Sibyl, Daughter-in-Law of Noah)
nodes.role: Prophetess of Sibylline Oracles Book III (Charles Vol. 2)
sources: R.H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Claims lineage inside Noah's Ark while prophesying the fall of Babel, Kronos-Titan, and Hellenistic empires.

nodes.name: Vita Adae et Evae (Apocalypse of Moses — Seth's Clay & Stone Tablets)
nodes.role: Adamic Penitence & Antediluvian Wisdom Literature (Charles Vol. 2)
sources: R.H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Records Seth and Eve inscribing Adamic history on clay and stone pillars against fire and Flood.

nodes.name: Judge Kenaz (1st Great Post-Joshua Judge) & Zebul in Pseudo-Philo
nodes.role: Kenezite Champion & Builder of Gilgal Sanctuary (LAB Ch. 25-29)
sources: Pseudo-Philo, Liber Antiquitatum Biblicarum (LAB)
nodes.notes: Liber Antiquitatum Biblicarum elevates Kenaz (brother of Caleb, father of Othniel) into a major forty-year judge.

nodes.name: Seila (Daughter of Judge Jephthah of Gilead) in Pseudo-Philo
nodes.role: Named Daughter of Jephthah & Mourner of Mount Stelac (LAB Ch. 40)
sources: Pseudo-Philo, Liber Antiquitatum Biblicarum (LAB)
nodes.notes: Pseudo-Philo gives Jephthah's unnamed biblical daughter the name Seila and preserves her lament.

nodes.name: Eluma (Daughter of Remac, Mother of Judge Samson) in Pseudo-Philo
nodes.role: Wife of Manoah of Zorah & Mother of Samson (LAB Ch. 42)
sources: Pseudo-Philo, Liber Antiquitatum Biblicarum (LAB)
nodes.notes: Liber Antiquitatum Biblicarum supplies the personal name Eluma for Samson's Danite mother.

nodes.name: Bochart's Phaleg (Peleg Partition of Mankind)
nodes.role: Foundational Comparative Ethnology of Genesis 10-11
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Samuel Bochart's Phaleg (1646) systematically mapped every Genesis 10 ethnonym across Semitic, Phoenician, and Greco-Latin sources.

nodes.name: Phoenician Colonies of Gades & Tartessus (Iberian West)
nodes.role: Sidonian-Tarshish Atlantic Ports Analyzed in Bochart Chanaan I
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Traces Phoenician Gadira (Cadiz) and Tartessus back to Tyrian-Sidonian navigation and Biblical Tarshish.

nodes.name: Phoenician Utica, Hippo & Leptis Magna (Libyan Coast)
nodes.role: Pre-Carthaginian Punic Foundations (Bochart Chanaan I.24)
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Documents early Sidonian-Tyrian settlements along Tunisia and Tripolitania.

nodes.name: Punic Sardinia (Nora/Sulci), Sicily & Melita/Malta
nodes.role: Central Mediterranean Punic-Canaanite Chain (Bochart)
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Maps Canaanite toponyms across Sicily (Panormus, Lilybaeum), Sardinia, and Malta.

nodes.name: Cassiterides (Atlantic Tin Islands) & Himilco Horizon
nodes.role: Northern Phoenician Maritime Trade in Bochart Chanaan I.39
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Bochart traced the Greek name 'Bretannike' and tin-trade terms to Phoenician/Punic Barat-anac.

nodes.name: Ashkenaz = Ascania / Phrygia & Lake Ascanius (Bochart)
nodes.role: Anatolian Localization of Ashkenaz son of Gomer
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Bochart demonstrated Homer's Ascanius and the Black Sea ('Axenos / Euxinus') preserve Ashkenaz in Phrygia-Bithynia.

nodes.name: Riphath (Paphlagonia) & Togarmah (Cappadocia-Armenia)
nodes.role: Gomerian Black Sea & Anatolian Lines in Bochart Phaleg III
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Correlated Riphath with Rhebas/Riphaei and Togarmah with Cappadocian horse-breeding tribes (Ezekiel 27:14).

nodes.name: Dodanim / Rodanim (Rhodes) & Elisah (Hellas/Peloponnese)
nodes.role: Ionian-Aegean Branches of Javan in Bochart Phaleg III.4-6
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Linked Rhodanim with Rhodes and Elishah with Elis / Alashiya purple-dye ports.

nodes.name: Targumic Table: Germania (Gomer), Afriki & Dardania
nodes.role: Aramaic Ethnographic Glosses on Japheth's Sons (Etheridge)
sources: J.W. Etheridge, The Targums of Onkelos and Jonathan ben Uzziel
nodes.notes: Targum Pseudo-Jonathan renders Gomer/Riphath/Ashkenaz as Phrygia, Parthia, Asia, Germania, and Barbaria.

nodes.name: Targumic Tiras = Thrace & Meshech = Mysia / Moesia
nodes.role: Aramaic Balkano-Anatolian Identifications (Etheridge)
sources: J.W. Etheridge, The Targums of Onkelos and Jonathan ben Uzziel
nodes.notes: Etheridge's Targum translates Tiras as Thrace (Tarkia) and Tubal as Bithynia/Iberia.

nodes.name: Targumic Shinar (Babel), Nisibis, Edessa & Ctesiphon
nodes.role: Mesopotamian Civic Identifications of Nimrod's Kingdom
sources: J.W. Etheridge, The Targums of Onkelos and Jonathan ben Uzziel
nodes.notes: Targum identifies Erech with Uruk/Edessa, Accad with Nisibis, and Calneh with Ctesiphon.

nodes.name: Targumic Caphtorim = Cappadocians & Casluhim = Pentapolitans
nodes.role: Aramaic Rendition of Mizraim's Coastal Offshoots
sources: J.W. Etheridge, The Targums of Onkelos and Jonathan ben Uzziel
nodes.notes: Both Onkelos and Pseudo-Jonathan render Caphtorim as Cappadocians (Kaputka'i) and Pathrusim as Pelusiotes.

nodes.name: Bochart's Two Ophirs (Yemen Saphar & Indian Taprobane)
nodes.role: Bochart's Synthesis of Arabian & Maritime Ophir
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Phaleg II.27 resolves Cassis/Sabaean Ophir in Arabia alongside the Red Sea-Indian Ocean trade.

nodes.name: Put (Phut) = Libya, Phut River & Mauretania (Bochart)
nodes.role: North African Localization of Ham's Third Son
sources: Samuel Bochart, Geographia Sacra seu Phaleg et Chanaan (Opera Omnia)
nodes.notes: Bochart cited Ptolemy, Pliny, and Jerome's Mauretanian 'Flumen Fut' to localize Phut across northwest Africa.

nodes.name: Pericles of Athens & Aspasia of Miletus
nodes.role: Alcmaeonid Statesman of the Athenian Golden Age
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Great-nephew of Cleisthenes; led the Delian League empire and delivered the Funeral Oration in Thucydides Book II.

nodes.name: King Archidamus II of Sparta (Son of Zeuxidamus)
nodes.role: Eurypontid King of Sparta & Commander of Archidamian War
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Eurypontid grandfather of Agesilaus II; counseled Spartan caution in Thucydides Book I.

nodes.name: Cleon & General Demosthenes of Athens
nodes.role: Victors of Sphacteria / Pylos (425 BCE)
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Captured the Spartan garrison at Sphacteria before falling respectively at Amphipolis and Syracuse.

nodes.name: Brasidas son of Tellis (Spartan Victor at Amphipolis)
nodes.role: Spartan General & Liberator of Chalcidice
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Reversed Athenian fortunes in northern Greece until the Peace of Nicias in Thucydides Books IV-V.

nodes.name: Nicias son of Niceratus (Athenian General & Peace Architect)
nodes.role: Negotiator of the Peace of Nicias (421 BCE)
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Led Athens' cautious oligarchic-conservative faction until the Sicilian catastrophe in Thucydides VII.

nodes.name: Hermocrates son of Hermon (Strategos of Syracuse)
nodes.role: Defender of Syracuse & Father-in-Law of Dionysius I
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Rallied Sicily at Gela (424 BCE) and repulsed the Athenian armada alongside Gylippus.

nodes.name: King Sitalces of the Odrysian Kingdom (Thrace)
nodes.role: Allied King of Thrace & Uncle of Seuthes I
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Concluded Athenian citizenship alliance (Sadocus) and marched 150,000 warriors into Macedonia (Thucydides II.95-101).

nodes.name: King Perdiccas II of Macedon (Son of Alexander I)
nodes.role: Argead King of Macedonia & Ancestor of Philip II
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Navigated Athens, Brasidas, and Thrace across twenty years of Peloponnesian diplomacy (Thucydides Books I-V).

nodes.name: Thucydides son of Olorus (Strategos & Historian)
nodes.role: Athenian General Related to Miltiades & Thracian Princes
sources: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War (1753)
nodes.notes: Connected by Thracian royal kin to Cimon and Miltiades; composed history of the Peloponnesian War in exile.

nodes.name: Strategos Aratus of Sicyon (Architect of the Achaean League)
nodes.role: Sixteen-Time Strategos of the Achaean Confederation
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Liberated Corinth's Acrocorinth and steered Achaean federal politics throughout Polybius Books II-VIII.

nodes.name: Philopoemen of Megalopolis ('Last of the Greeks')
nodes.role: Eight-Time Achaean Strategos & Mentor of Polybius
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Reformed Achaean phalanx and cavalry; defeated Machanidas and Nabis of Sparta in Polybius.

nodes.name: King Philip V of Macedon (Antigonid Adversary of Rome)
nodes.role: Antigonid King of Macedonia (221 - 179 BCE)
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Great-grandson of Antigonus I; allied with Hannibal before fighting Flamininus at Cynoscephalae (197 BCE).

nodes.name: King Perseus of Macedon (Last Antigonid King)
nodes.role: Final Reigning Sovereign of Alexander's Homeland
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Son of Philip V defeated by Aemilius Paullus at Pydna (168 BCE), ending the Macedonian monarchy.

nodes.name: King Hiero II of Syracuse & Archimedes
nodes.role: 54-Year Constitutional King of Syracuse & His Kinsman-Geometer
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Preserved Syracuse's prosperity between Rome and Carthage for half a century; praised by Polybius Book VII.

nodes.name: King Masinissa of Unified Numidia
nodes.role: Massylian King of Numidia & Zama Ally of Scipio Africanus
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Son of King Gaia; commanded the Numidian cavalry winning Zama (202 BCE) and unified Numidia for 54 years.

nodes.name: King Syphax of the Masaesyli (West Numidia)
nodes.role: West Numidian Sovereign & Husband of Sophonisba
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Negotiated simultaneously with Scipio Africanus and Hasdrubal Gisco in Polybius Book XIV.

nodes.name: Kings Attalus I Soter & Eumenes II of Pergamon
nodes.role: Attalid Builders of the Great Altar & Library of Pergamon
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Defeated the Galatians, allied with Rome against Antiochus III, and made Pergamon the cultural jewel of Anatolia.

nodes.name: Polybius of Megalopolis (Son of Lycortas, Mentor of Scipio Aemilianus)
nodes.role: Achaean Hipparch & Universal Historian of Rome's Rise
sources: Polybius, The General History of Polybius
nodes.notes: Achaean hostage in Rome who accompanied Scipio Aemilianus to Carthage (146 BCE) and framed universal constitutional history.

nodes.name: King Vercingetorix of the Arverni (Son of Celtillus)
nodes.role: Unified Commander of the Gallic Coalition (52 BCE)
sources: Julius Caesar, The Commentaries (Gallic & Civil Wars, 1753)
nodes.notes: Defended Gergovia and Alesia against Julius Caesar in De Bello Gallico Book VII.

nodes.name: King Ariovistus of the Suebi (Rex Germanorum)
nodes.role: Suebic King Across the Rhine & Friend of the Roman Senate
sources: Julius Caesar, The Commentaries (Gallic & Civil Wars, 1753)
John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Entered Alsace at Sequanian invitation before fighting Julius Caesar at Vosges (58 BCE).

nodes.name: King Cassivellaunus of the Catuvellauni (Britain 54 BCE)
nodes.role: High War-Leader of Southeastern Britons Against Caesar
sources: Julius Caesar, The Commentaries (Gallic & Civil Wars, 1753)
nodes.notes: Opposed Caesar's Thames crossing in De Bello Gallico Book V; ancestor of Tasciovanus and Cunobelinus.

nodes.name: Kings Ambiorix & Catuvolcus of the Eburones
nodes.role: Belgic Dual Kings of the Ardennes / Meuse
sources: Julius Caesar, The Commentaries (Gallic & Civil Wars, 1753)
nodes.notes: Co-kings of the Germani Cisrhenani / Eburones who destroyed Atuatuca garrison in De Bello Gallico V-VI.

nodes.name: Druid Diviciacus & Chief Dumnorix of the Aedui
nodes.role: Aeduan Vergobret Brothers & Diplomatic Bridge to Cicero
sources: Julius Caesar, The Commentaries (Gallic & Civil Wars, 1753)
nodes.notes: Diviciacus addressed the Roman Senate and befriended Cicero; Dumnorix wed Orgetorix's daughter.

nodes.name: King Commius of the Atrebates (Gaul & Britain)
nodes.role: Founder of British Atrebatic Kingdom (Calleva/Silchester)
sources: Julius Caesar, The Commentaries (Gallic & Civil Wars, 1753)
nodes.notes: Served first as Caesar's British envoy before founding the Atrebatic dynasty of Tincomarus in southern Britain.

nodes.name: Orgetorix of the Helvetii (+ Alpine Princes)
nodes.role: Wealthiest Helvetian Nobleman & Initiator of 58 BCE Migration
sources: Julius Caesar, The Commentaries (Gallic & Civil Wars, 1753)
nodes.notes: Forged marriage alliance with Dumnorix of the Aedui and Casticus of the Sequani in De Bello Gallico I.2-4.

nodes.name: Prince Arminius (Hermann) of the Cherusci (Teutoburg 9 CE)
nodes.role: Cheruscan Prince, Roman Eques & Victor of Teutoburg Forest
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Son of Segimer; halted Roman provincial expansion at the Weser/Rhine across Mascou Book IV.

nodes.name: Princess Thusnelda, Segestes & Thumelicus of the Cherusci
nodes.role: Bride of Arminius & Captive Cheruscan Royalty at Ravenna
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Mascou Book IV highlights Thusnelda's dignity alongside Germanicus's Elbe campaigns.

nodes.name: King Maroboduus of the Marcomanni (Bohemia Confederation)
nodes.role: Organizer of the Central European Marcomannic Kingdom
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Raised in Augustus's Rome before building a 74,000-man Germanic kingdom in Boiohaemum (Bohemia).

nodes.name: Gaius Julius Civilis (Batavian Revolt Leader, 69 - 70 CE)
nodes.role: Batavian Royal Prince & Former Roman Auxiliary Prefect
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Rallied Batavi, Canninefates, Bructeri (Prophetess Veleda), and Gauls along the Lower Rhine in Mascou Book IV.

nodes.name: Gothic Kings Cniva (250 CE) & Fritigern (Adrianople 378 CE)
nodes.role: Danubian Gothic Commanders in Mascou Books V & VII
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Cniva defeated Decius at Abritus (251 CE); Fritigern led Thervingi across the Danube in 376-378 CE.

nodes.name: King Radagaisus & Magister Militum Flavius Stilicho
nodes.role: Gothic Invader of Fiesole & Vandal-Roman Regent of Honorius
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Mascou Book VIII profiles Stilicho (half-Vandal regent married to Serena, niece of Theodosius I).

nodes.name: King Odoacer of Italy (476 - 493 CE)
nodes.role: Scirian-Torcilingian King Ending the Western Roman Office (476 CE)
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Son of Ediko; deposed Romulus Augustulus and governed Italy seventeen years until Theoderic (Mascou Book X).

nodes.name: King Gundobad of Burgundy (Lex Burgundionum, r. 473 - 516 CE)
nodes.role: Burgundian Lawgiver King & Uncle of Queen Clotilde
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Codified the Lex Gundobada (Loi Gombette); niece Clotilde married Clovis I, founding Christian Francia.

nodes.name: Duke Widukind of Saxony (Contender Against Charlemagne)
nodes.role: Saxon Ducal Leader & Ancestor of the Ottonians & Savoy
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Led Saxon resistance for eight years before accepting baptism at Attigny (785 CE).

nodes.name: Duke Tassilo III of Bavaria (Agilolfing Dynasty)
nodes.role: Agilolfing Sovereign Duke of Bavaria & Son-in-Law of Desiderius
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Cousin of Charlemagne married to Liutperga of Lombardy; presided over late Agilolfing Bavarian law.

nodes.name: Queen Boudica of the Iceni & King Caratacus
nodes.role: British Sovereign Resistance Leaders Against Claudius & Nero
sources: John Jacob Mascou, The History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
Tacitus, Agricola & Annals; British Chronicles
nodes.notes: Caratacus led the Catuvellauni-Silures resistance; Queen Boudica led the 60/61 CE East Anglian uprising.

nodes.name: King Lha Lama Yeshe-O of Guge (Founder of Tholing, c. 966 - 1036 CE)
nodes.role: Monk-King of Western Tibet & Second Diffusion Pioneer
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Skyid-lde Nyi-ma-mgon; funded Rinchen Zangpo and sacrificed himself ransom-free to summon Atisha.

nodes.name: King Jangchub-O & Lha-lde of Guge (+ Atisha Dipamkara, 1042 CE)
nodes.role: Nephew of Yeshe-O & Patron of Lamp for the Path
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Welcomed Bengal master Atisha Dipamkara Shrijnana to Tholing Monastery in 1042 CE.

nodes.name: Lotsawa Rinchen Zangpo ('Great Translator' of Tabo & Alchi, 958 - 1055 CE)
nodes.role: Founder of 108 Western Himalayan Monasteries
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Trained in Kashmir and established Tabo, Tholing, and Alchi under Guge royal patronage (Francke Vol. 1).

nodes.name: King Detsugon of Zanskar & Spiti (Son of Nyima-Gon)
nodes.role: Founder of Zanskar & Spiti Royal Branch
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Youngest son of Nyi-ma-mgon awarded Zanskar, Spiti, and Lahaul in Francke's La-dvags rgyal-rabs.

nodes.name: King Lhachen Utpala of Ladakh (c. 1080 - 1110 CE)
nodes.role: Conqueror of Kullu, Purang & Baltistan
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Chronicles of Ladakh (Francke Vol. 2) credit Utpala with subjugating Kullu and extracting annual treaties.

nodes.name: Kings Lhachen Naglug & Joldor (Builders of Wanla & Khalatse Bridge)
nodes.role: Early Lhachen Kings of Lower Ladakh
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Constructed the stone-anchored Indus bridge at Khalatse and fortress of Wanla recorded in Francke Vol. 1.

nodes.name: King Tashi Namgyal of Ladakh (Founder of Leh Tsemo, r. 1555 - 1575 CE)
nodes.role: Grandson of King Bhagan & Defender Against Mirza Haidar Dughlat
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Built Namgyal Tsemo monastery above Leh after repelling Central Asian horsemen.

nodes.name: King Tsewang Namgyal I of Ladakh (r. 1575 - 1595 CE)
nodes.role: Nephew of Tashi Namgyal & Western Himalayan Suzerain
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Restored Ladakhi authority from Guge and Purang down to Mustang before Jamyang and Sengge Namgyal.

nodes.name: King Deldan Namgyal of Ladakh (+ Queen Kalzang Dolma, r. 1642 - 1694)
nodes.role: Eldest Son of Sengge Namgyal & Builder of Shey Chorten
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Maintained Leh sovereignty during the 1679-1684 Tibet-Ladakh-Mughal treaty at Tingmosgang.

nodes.name: King Nyima Namgyal of Ladakh (Printer of Kanjur, r. 1694 - 1729)
nodes.role: Scholar-King & Patron of Leh Printing Blocks
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Issued copper charters preserved and translated across Francke Vol. 2.

nodes.name: King Tsepal Tondup Namgyal (Last Independent Gyalpo of Ladakh, r. 1802 - 1834)
nodes.role: Final Namgyal Sovereign Before Dogra General Zorawar Singh
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Built Stok Palace as royal residence of the Namgyal house; descendants retain Stok title into modern times.

nodes.name: Nono Hereditary Chiefs of Spiti (Tabo & Dhankar)
nodes.role: Hereditary Wazirs of Spiti Valley
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Francke Vol. 1 traces the Nono house of Kyuling safeguarding Tabo's millennium-old frescoes.

nodes.name: Rajas Kehri Singh & Shamsher Singh of Bashahr (Kinnaur, 1684 Treaty)
nodes.role: Highland Rajput-Himalayan Kings of Rampur Bashahr
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Allied with Ladakh and Lhasa in the 1684 Sutlej trade treaty recorded in Francke Vol. 1 & 2.

nodes.name: Makpon Ali Sher Khan Anchan of Skardu (Baltistan, c. 1590 - 1625 CE)
nodes.role: Unifier of Baltistan & Father-in-Law of Sengge Namgyal
sources: A.H. Francke, Antiquities of Indian Tibet Vols. 1-2 (ASI New Imperial Series)
nodes.notes: Married his daughter Gyal Khatun to Jamyang Namgyal, bearing Ladakh's 'Lion King' Sengge Namgyal.

nodes.name: Kings Sancho I ('The Populator') & Afonso II of Portugal
nodes.role: Burgundian Kings of Early Portugal (1185 - 1223 CE)
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Son and grandson of Afonso I Henriques who consolidated the Tagus valley and convened the Cortes of Coimbra.

nodes.name: King Afonso III 'the Boulonnais' (Conqueror of the Algarve)
nodes.role: King of Portugal & the Algarve (r. 1248 - 1279 CE)
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Fixed Portugal's continental borders and fathered King Dinis.

nodes.name: Kings Afonso IV, Pedro I & Ines de Castro of Portugal
nodes.role: Fathers of the House of Aviz (Rio Salado 1340)
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Fought at Salado alongside Alfonso XI of Castile; Pedro I's son John I founded the House of Aviz.

nodes.name: King Duarte I & Regent Dom Pedro, Duke of Coimbra
nodes.role: Sons of King John I & Queen Philippa of Lancaster
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Brothers of Henry the Navigator bridging Aviz exploration and European courts.

nodes.name: King John II ('The Perfect Prince', Bartolomeu Dias 1488)
nodes.role: Son of Afonso V; Sponsor of the Cape of Good Hope & Tordesillas
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Centralized royal finances and dispatched Bartolomeu Dias and Pero da Covilha toward India.

nodes.name: Kings John III, Sebastian (Alcacer Quibir 1578) & Cardinal Henry I
nodes.role: Final Aviz Kings Before the Iberian Union (1580)
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Anchored Portugal's Asian empire at Goa/Malacca prior to the 1580 succession crisis.

nodes.name: Queen Catherine of Braganza (Wife of Charles II of England)
nodes.role: Daughter of King John IV of Portugal & Regent of Portugal
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Brought Bombay and Tangier in Anglo-Portuguese alliance; ruled as Regent of Portugal in 1704-1705.

nodes.name: King Jose I (+ Marquis de Pombal) & Queen Maria I of Portugal
nodes.role: 18th-Century Braganza Sovereigns of Portugal & Brazil
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
A Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal
nodes.notes: Led Lisbon's post-1755 Enlightenment reconstruction and erected Brazil to a united kingdom.

nodes.name: Queen Fredegund of Neustria (Consort of Chilperic I & Mother of Chlothar II)
nodes.role: Merovingian Regent Queen of Neustria (Mezeray 1683)
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Governing Queen of Neustria and fierce rival of Brunhilda across Mezeray's First Race (561-597 CE); mother of Chlothar II.

nodes.name: Pepin of Herstal & Mayor Charles Martel (Victor of Tours, 732 CE)
nodes.role: Carolingian Mayors of the Palace & Grandfather of Charlemagne
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Pepin of Herstal unified Austrasia-Neustria after Merovingian ascendancy; his son Charles Martel won Tours/Poitiers (732 CE).

nodes.name: Kings Louis VI ('the Fat') & Louis VII (+ Abbot Suger)
nodes.role: Consolidators of the Ile-de-France & Second Crusade
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Secured the royal demesne around Paris and Saint-Denis, fathering Philip II Augustus.

nodes.name: King Philip IV ('the Fair') & Isabella 'She-Wolf' of France
nodes.role: Capetian Grandson of St. Louis IX & Father of Last Direct Capetians
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Presided over Estates-General (1302) and Avignon Papacy transition; daughter Isabella carried English claim to Valois.

nodes.name: King John II, Charles V ('the Wise') & Bertrand du Guesclin
nodes.role: Valois Kings & Breton Constable of France
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Recovered French provinces after Bretigny and endowed the Louvre Royal Library.

nodes.name: King Charles VII ('the Victorious') & St. Joan of Arc (Orleans 1429)
nodes.role: Crowned at Reims (1429 CE) & Winner of the Hundred Years' War
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Crowned through Joan of Arc's relief of Orleans and Formigny/Castillon campaigns in Mezeray Book II.

nodes.name: King Louis XI ('the Prudent / Universal Spider') of France
nodes.role: Unifier of Burgundy, Anjou, Maine & Provence into Crownlands
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Built France's centralized Valois monarchy by absorbing Charles the Bold's Burgundian heritage.

nodes.name: Kings Francis I, Henry II & Queen Catherine de' Medici
nodes.role: Renaissance Valois-Angouleme Monarchs of France
sources: Francois Eudes de Mezeray, General Chronological History of France (1683)
nodes.notes: Patrons of Leonardo da Vinci and Chambord; married Valois children across Scotland, Spain, and Navarre.

nodes.name: Kings Edgar 'the Peaceful', Ethelred II & Edmund Ironside
nodes.role: Late Anglo-Saxon Kings of All England (Strutt 1779)
sources: Joseph Strutt, Chronicle of England / Ancient Britons and Saxons (1779)
nodes.notes: Great-grandsons of Alfred the Great covered in Strutt's 1779 Chronicle from Bath's 973 coronation to Assandun.

nodes.name: King Harold II Godwinson & Edgar the Aetheling (+ St. Margaret of Scotland)
nodes.role: Final Anglo-Saxon Kings & Scottish-English Bridge Princess
sources: Joseph Strutt, Chronicle of England / Ancient Britons and Saxons (1779)
nodes.notes: Edgar's sister St. Margaret wed Malcolm III Canmore, carrying Wessex blood into all later British monarchs.
